column1: # Cross-check mapping: this parser's diagnostic codes against net-snmp's
# MIB parser, as read by reference_test.go.
# Tab-separated. Two record kinds:
#   map<TAB>fixture<TAB>code<TAB>fragment
#       In testdata/malformed/<fixture>, this parser's <code> and any
#       net-snmp message whose text holds <fragment> are a claim about the
#       same construct. The test requires both sides to name the same
#       declaration, not merely to have said something.
#   differ<TAB>fixture<TAB>code<TAB>fragment<TAB>ours<TAB>theirs
#       Both parsers grade the condition and each puts its finger on a
#       different declaration. The row pins both constructs, so a
#       disagreement is asserted rather than excused: if either side
#       moves, the row fails and the adjudication is redone. The comment
#       above each row is that adjudication.
#   none<TAB>code<TAB>reason
#       net-snmp has no counterpart for <code>. Every catalog code must
#       appear in one half or the other, so a code with no counterpart is
#       a written-down fact rather than a silent gap.
# Fragments are net-snmp message text and will move between releases.
# Written against NET-SNMP 5.6.2.1; a fragment that stops matching fails
# loudly rather than passing, which is the point.
# net-snmp is run without -Pu on purpose. Allowing underscores in
# descriptors is one of the tolerances under comparison here, so asking
# the reference to tolerate it too would delete the only row that grades
# it.
map

column1: # The four rows below are disagreements about where the fault lives, not
# about whether there is one. Each names the RFC clause it was decided
# against.
# The separator is five hyphens: ASN.1 pairs them off into an empty
# comment and leaves one minus behind (RFC 2578 section 3.7 ends a
# comment at a second pair of hyphens or at end of line). The construct
# at fault is the separator line. net-snmp reports the stray minus only
# where its parser reaches it, which by then is the next declaration, so
# it names plain. This parser is right on position.
differ
column3: smi/hyphen-separator

column1: # RFC 2578 states no acyclicity requirement on IMPORTS; a cycle only
# leaves the load with no acyclic order. This parser grades the IMPORTS
# statement that closes the cycle and keeps both modules. net-snmp has no
# message about the cycle at all — it loads A-MIB first, cannot resolve
# bRoot, and reports the consequence on aLeaf, which it then drops. This
# parser is right: the construct at fault is the back edge, and losing a
# declaration over it is not something the RFC asks for.
differ
column3: smi/import-cycle

column1: # RFC 2578 section 3.2 requires every external descriptor to be reached
# through IMPORTS, and the construct that breaks the rule is the use:
# sysName's SYNTAX names DisplayString on line 6. net-snmp reports it
# there. This parser raises the diagnostic during resolution, where the
# only position it has is the module, so it points at line 1 and names
# the symbol in the message text instead. net-snmp is right on position;
# a reader fixing this wants the line that uses the type.
differ
column3: smi/missing-import

column1: # RFC 2578 section 3.7 delimits a text value with quotation marks, so the
# construct at fault is runaway's DESCRIPTION, where the opening quote
# is. net-snmp reports at line 11, one past the last line of the file:
# that is where it noticed, not where the fault is. This parser is right
# on position.
differ
column3: smi/unterminated-string
